messages:
Marie: kicked off the nightly perf-sampler job an hour ago, noticed an unexpected kernel selection shift on A100s — cudnn conv -> custom_gemm for several conv ops. uploading full traces to s3://redwood-ci/perf/2026/171950/ :mag:
perf-bot: job #4212 finished, artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/perf/2026/171950/job-4212/{nsys.qdrep, kernel_timeline.csv, kernel_histogram.json} :white_check_mark:
Raj: which commit/PR did the job pick up? could be the compile-time kernel selection heuristic from last week
Marie: it used commit 9f3b2c1 (PR #2243) — the selector change is in runtime/compile/kernel_selector.cc: added seq_len skew heuristic
Sam: can you paste a small snippet of the kernel timeline or the nsys command you used? heatmap diffs are the easiest to reason about
Marie: sure, nsys command I ran locally before uploading: ```nsys profile -o job4212 --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu  --stats=true --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx``` then `nsys export -f csv -o kernel_timeline job4212.qdrep`
Tess: thanks. do we also have the nvtx ranges annotated for batching boundaries? that helps separate model init vs steady-state
Marie: yes I annotated batch boundaries in the sampler with nvtx push/pop, you'll see `BATCH_START`/`BATCH_END` markers in the timeline csv
Olga: quick stat check: kv-cache miss rate in that run jumped ~3.1% vs baseline (from 1.8% -> 4.9%). that can change effective seq_len distribution which the selector uses, so two hypotheses: selector heuristic or KV miss spike changing observed inputs
Raj: good catch. two follow-ups: 1) rerun with a stable KV prefetch config to isolate kernel selector effect; 2) collect a smaller targeted nsys with `--sample-policy=kvcache-aware` to bias sampling to cache-sensitive paths
Marie: re-run queued with `--sample-policy=kvcache-aware --sample-rate=0.25` (smaller timeframe, but focused). I'll also upload both the raw .qdrep and the exported csv + kernel_histogram.json so diff runner can parse
Sam: for the diff dashboard we want both histograms and a per-kernel p95 latency table. current pipeline compresses qdrep -> qdzp which loses the csv export step sometimes — suggest pipeline preserves exported csv and kernel_histogram.json explicitly
Tess: agree. can we make the uploader save `kernel_histogram.json` and `kv_cache_fingerprint.txt` to the artifact bucket as part of the same job? then the diff tool can bucket-by-fingerprint and do meaningful comparisons
Marie: drafting a small change to the nightly perf job: 1) run `nsys export --output kernel_timeline.csv job4212.qdrep` 2) run `python infra/tools/kernel_histogram.py --input kernel_timeline.csv --output kernel_histogram.json` 3) upload both files to s3. pushing PR to infra/perf-ci now
Raj: also add an automated check in the pipeline that fails CI if the kernel selection distribution shifts >2% for production kernels (we already have similar gate for p50/p95 but not for kernel labels)
perf-bot: new ticket PERF-1127 created and assigned to Marie: "nightly perf: persist kernel_histogram + kv fingerprints, add kernel-distribution gate" :ticket:
Sam: once PR is up, I'll add dashboard ingestion hook to parse kernel_histogram.json and render a sparklines + heatmap tile. link to example dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/dashboards/kernel-heatmap
Marie: PR opened: infra/ci#318 — changes: preserve csv, upload histograms, add `--kvcache-prefetch` toggle for sampler. will run a backfill for last 7 nightly runs so we get historical diffs
Olga: can you also attach the small repro trace where we force the kv miss? a short trace (30s) is easier to eyeball for kernel selection differences
Marie: yes I'll attach a 30s capture as job4212-small.qdrep to the PR artifacts
Tess: nit: in the pipeline uploader, gzip kernel_histogram.json but keep the original filename so dashboard code picks it up automatically (avoid renaming to .json.gz)
Marie: noted. action items: - push PR (done) - run backfill for 7 nights (queued) - attach small repro capture (will do) - follow up with perf diff screenshot in this thread.
Raj: thanks — once backfill is in, let's run the histogram diff job and if the >2% gate fires we triage whether selector or input distribution is root cause. :eyes:
perf-bot: backfill job queued (#4213). ETA ~45m. artifacts at s3://redwood-ci/perf/2026/171950/backfill-4213/
Marie: thanks all — will post the first histogram diff when backfill completes.
